The `PosixParser` class in `org.apache.commons.cli` has a `parse` method that is responsible for parsing command line arguments. The `parse` method takes in options, arguments, properties, and a boolean flag `stopAtNonOption` to control behavior.

Based on the description in the current bug report, it seems that the issue lies in how the `PosixParser` handles unrecognized tokens starting with '-' when the `stopAtNonOption` flag is enabled. The bug report mentions that these unrecognized tokens are simply being ignored instead of being handled properly.

Looking at the `parse` method implementation, we can see that when processing each token in the command line arguments:
- If a token starts with '-' and is not recognized as an option, and the `stopAtNonOption` flag is enabled, the parser simply adds the token to the command line without further processing. This behavior leads to unrecognized tokens being ignored.
- There is no specific handling for unrecognized tokens starting with '-' when the `stopAtNonOption` flag is enabled.

To address this issue, the `PosixParser` class needs to be modified to properly handle unrecognized tokens starting with '-' when the `stopAtNonOption` flag is enabled. This can be done by adjusting the logic in the `parse` method to ensure that unrecognized tokens are not ignored but are processed accordingly based on the specified behavior.

Based on the provided information, the root cause of the bug is the incomplete handling of unrecognized tokens in the `PosixParser` class.

Next, I will provide the methods that should be fixed to address this bug.
```
org.apache.commons.cli.Parser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], boolean)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
